learningObjective: Explain GPTQ's central technique: per-layer weight quantization via second-order (Hessian-inverse-based) error compensation.
stem: GPTQ (Frantar et al., ICLR 2023) is a PTQ algorithm that quantizes LLM weights to INT4 with small accuracy loss. Which best captures its central technique?

options.text: GPTQ quantizes weights column-by-column, and after each column's quantization it updates the remaining unquantized columns using the Hessian of the per-layer reconstruction error (approximated as `H = 2 X^T X` from calibration activations); this compensates for the just-introduced quantization error and dramatically improves the fit versus naive round-to-nearest.
GPTQ retrains the entire model with a straight-through estimator on the quantized weights; it is essentially QAT with a specific initializer.
GPTQ uses reinforcement learning to search for optimal per-tensor scales; the 'GPT' in the name refers to a GPT-2 policy network.
GPTQ is a runtime dequantization technique that computes INT4 → FP16 dequants faster than standard kernels; it does not change how weights are quantized offline.

explanation: GPTQ's core technique is a per-layer optimization: quantize one column of the weight matrix at a time, then use the (once-computed) Cholesky-inverse of the Hessian of the reconstruction error to update the still-unquantized columns to compensate for the introduced error. This is a second-order variant of OBS/OBQ adapted for LLM-scale weight matrices. It runs offline (no full model training) and produces INT4 weights with 1-4% perplexity increase on 175B-parameter models. Options B, C, D are unrelated inventions.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: matches GPTQ paper's algorithm description.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: GPTQ is PTQ, not QAT.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: 'GPT' refers to the target model class (GPT-family), not RL.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: GPTQ is an offline quantization algorithm.

assumptions: The layer is a linear layer with a computable per-layer Hessian.
A calibration set of activations is available.
nonImplications: Does not imply GPTQ handles activation outliers — it focuses purely on weight quantization; W4A16 is its typical deployment.
Does not imply GPTQ is the only choice; AWQ and RTN are alternatives with different trade-offs.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses offline algorithm with runtime kernel.

sourceRefs.locator: Sections 3-4: algorithm description and Hessian update rule
